mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 3.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising real discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in UNRATE below 5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening labor demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST below 2000 for four consecutive months signals weakening housing demand, which negatively impacts construction and home-related consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in INDPRO above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in industrial production, reflecting robust supply growth and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between GDPC1 and RSAFS where GDPC1 grows faster than RSAFS by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a divergence between aggregate demand and personal savings, suggesting increased consumption and potential overextension, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise simultaneously above their respective 12-month averages for two consecutive months, it signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, increasing recession risk and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo avg AND CPIAUCSL > 12-mo avg for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between PAYEMS growth and S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days exists during periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 5%), reflecting that labor market strength directly boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations.
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS growth and 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of low-unemployment months.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST and GDPC1 both decline for three consecutive months, it signals a coordinated weakening in housing demand and overall economic demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
